summary: Yale reads applications need-blind regardless of citizenship and meets 100% of demonstrated need with grants, not loans. For students entering in 2026–27 and later, families earning under $200,000 pay no tuition and those under $100,000 have the full cost covered.
covers: Need-blind admission for international applicants and 100% of demonstrated need met — no loans required.
Families with typical assets earning under $100,000: full cost of attendance covered, including tuition, housing and meals, with travel, hospitalisation insurance and a $2,000 start-up grant.
Families earning under $200,000: no tuition. Families between $75,000 and $200,000 typically pay between 0% and 10% of income.
eligibility: First-year applicants from any country applying to Yale College.
Aid is based on demonstrated need, assessed from family income and assets.
how_to_apply: Apply through one of the platforms Yale accepts, such as the Common Application or QuestBridge.
Choose Single-Choice Early Action (1 November) or Regular Decision (2 January).
Submit Yale's financial aid application materials (including the CSS Profile) by the aid deadlines.
Request an application fee waiver if the fee is a hardship.
watch_out: Single-Choice Early Action restricts other early applications — read the exceptions carefully.
The new income thresholds apply from the 2026–27 entering class; use Yale's net price calculator for your own estimate.
Admission is highly selective; balance your list with other full-need colleges.

sources.title: Yale News — Yale to offer free tuition to families with incomes below $200,000 (January 2026)
